newsitem.title: UK: Ex-minister backs Hague in UK Conservative race.
newsitem.headline: Ex-minister backs Hague in UK Conservative race.

text.p: Former Welsh secretary William Hague on Friday won the second important endorsement in as many days in his bid to become leader of the Conservative party when ex-Scottish secretary Michael Forsyth backed him for the job.

"The Conservative party neeeds a fresh start from a new generation. I believe the man to give the party that fresh start is William Hague," Forsyth, who lost his seat when the Conservatives were routed in the May 1 election, said.
Hague on Thursday bolstered his position as favourite in the six-man race to succeed John Major when former Northern Ireland minister Michael Ancram declared his support.

The first round of voting for the new leader among the Conservatives' 164 surviving members of parliament will be held on June 10. None of the contenders is expected to win outright on the first ballot. A second ballot is due the week after.

In remarks prepared for delivery to an expected audience of more than 500 Conservative members in Manchester later on Friday, Hague said the party had to seize a once in a lifetime opportunity to make a fresh start.

"Two years from now the words people associate with the Conservative party must not be 'sleaze' or 'greed' or 'division'. My ambition is that the words people associate with the Conservative party two years from now are the words 'fresh', 'clear', 'open' and 'united'," Hague said.

He proposed a thorough shake-up of the party machine, a recruitment drive to double membership in two years, closer consultation with party members over policy and a greater focus on local government.
"My objective is to rebuild the Conservative party to be the driving force in British politics once more," Hague said.
